prompt: I just inherited $175,000. I've been investing for a few years and have a simple three-fund portfolio. I'm terrified of putting it all in at once — what if the market crashes right after? My plan is to spread this out over 3 years, investing about $5,000 per month. Is that a good approach?
assertions: Claude cites Vanguard's research that lump-sum investing beats DCA roughly two-thirds of the time historically
Claude explicitly pushes back on the 3-year DCA plan as an unnecessarily long window with significant expected opportunity cost
Claude acknowledges the emotional difficulty of lump-sum investing and validates the anxiety without endorsing the 3-year plan
Claude recommends either lump-sum investing immediately or a compressed DCA schedule of 3-6 months (not 3 years) if anxiety is the primary concern
Claude frames the 3-year DCA plan as a form of market timing — waiting and hoping the market will be lower — rather than a sound financial strategy
